findings.title: Cleanup service ticker interval reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: `CleanUpService.Run` changes the cleanup ticker from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. This appears to be a leftover local testing change and causes all background cleanup jobs (annotations, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, user invites, short URLs, and query history) to run 10x more frequently than intended, while `clean()` still assumes a 10-minute period with `const timeout = 9 * time.Minute`.

findings.title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps ID slices on every cleanup batch
findings.body: `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579) call `r.log.Error` twice per batch even when no error occurred (on lines 534, 554, and 576 `err` is always `nil`) and even when `len(ids) == 0`. In addition, logging `"ids", ids` serializes the entire batch of annotation IDs into the error logs on every batch iteration, which will heavily spam production error logs.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when running on SQLite with a batch size above 999, `values` is built in a loop with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. This performs O(n^2) string copies and allocations over `len(ids)` (for example, with the tested batch size of 32,767, a single batch allocates hundreds of megabytes of intermediate strings). Additionally, the condition checks `r.cfg.AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > sqliteParameterLimit` instead of `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit`, so even small batches inline the IDs when a large batch size is configured. Use `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` (as done in `getAccessControlFilter` in this file) and check `len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit`.
